result.title: STRIDE: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Driving Edge Cases
result.summary: In autonomous driving, perceiving surrounding objects is not enough: failing to understand how they move and interact over time can lead to dangerous decisions. Evaluating vision-language models (VLMs) therefore requires testing whether they connect past spatial observations to future consequences. Yet existing benchmarks often assess edge cases through basic perception questions or test temporal understanding in simple scenarios, leaving complex spatiotemporal reasoning underexplored. We introduce STRIDE (SpatioTemporal Reasoning In Driving Edge Cases), an object-centric benchmark for long-tail, safety-critical driving scenarios. STRIDE covers six task families: spatial perception, spatial understanding, temporal memory, temporal extrapolation, trajectory prediction, and scene-context awareness. It pairs multiple-choice questions probing individual spatiotemporal judgments with related free-form visual question answering (VQA) requiring detailed scene explanations and justifications of driving decisions. We prioritize scenes with unusual object behaviors and complex traffic interactions, generate reference answers from structured dataset annotations through automated procedures, and use limited language-model assistance and human verification to ensure annotation quality. Across 12 proprietary, open-weight, and driving-specialized models, even the best performer, GPT-6-Astra, achieves only 43.4% average multiple-choice accuracy, versus an approximately 20% random-choice baseline. Further analysis reveals that strong performance in describing driving scenes does not necessarily translate to accurate safety-critical judgments, and that models struggle more with reconstructing object motion than recalling past positions. STRIDE thus exposes spatiotemporal driving limitations that aggregate VQA scores can conceal.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 STRIDE，一个面向自动驾驶长尾安全场景、以对象为中心的时空推理基准，涵盖空间感知、空间理解、时序记忆、时序外推、轨迹预测与场景语境六类任务，结合选择题与自由式 VQA；评测 12 个模型后发现最佳模型选择题平均准确率仅 43.4%，且善于描述场景并不等于判断可靠。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于 VLM 多模态推理的诊断性基准，其「重建物体运动比回忆过去位置更难」等结论可供核查时序记忆、状态更新与视觉证据使用方式，但未涉及 latent 推理状态生成，联系主要在评价与失败分析层面。
